James — thanks for the detailed questions. Answers below and I've attached a redlined addendum that reflects the cash-credit option for SLA failures and an optional 1500 tokens/sec tier pricing sheet.

1) Burst buffer: The 15% burst capacity is automatic for short spikes (defined as <= 2 minutes per occurrence) and happens transparently if available capacity exists in the reserved pool. For sustained bursts above 2 minutes, we rely on your burst credits or autoscaling capacity; during renewal we're recommending a +1 GPU burst reserve that can be consumed for sustained spikes.

2) SLA credit calc (cash option): monthly_credit = max(0, (1 - (minutes_meeting_slo / total_monitoring_minutes)) * monthly_reserved_fee * 0.5). This results in a cash refund up to 50% of the monthly reserved fee proportional to the SLO shortfall. The addendum includesWorkedExample A.

3) Measurement: We measure at the reserved pool level (aggregate tokens/sec across routes bound to that pool), normalized to 16kB context length. Per-model route exceptions: we can allow route-level exclusions on a case-by-case basis if you provide target prompts and traffic split.

Pricing delta: baseline (1200 tokens/sec) -> $45k/month reserved fee. Committed 1500 tokens/sec -> $58k/month. The pricing sheet in the attachments has a line-item breakdown and per-token cost for overage.

Next steps: Rafael will validate the technical calcs and Aditya will confirm GPU scaling numbers. If those checks look good, I'll post the addendum for signature.

Best,
Priya

Hi all — looping in a few technical details so procurement has confidence in the throughput numbers.

- The 4x A100-equivalent GPUs give ~1.2k tokens/sec baseline for the primary model mix (avg. 1.2kB prompt + 512 token responses at 16kB context) when using Redwood inference runtime with our standard KV caching and grouped batching.
- The automatic 15% burst is allowed only when the pool's unused GPU cycles exist; it does not preempt workloads on other dedicated pools. For guaranteed sustained uplift we recommend the +1 GPU burst reserve referenced by Priya.
- We instrument tokens/sec at the pool level every 10s and evaluate 5m rolling windows for SLO calculation. The normalization to 16kB context is applied by the telemetry layer; raw per-request runtime duration is also retained for debugging.

Edge cases to be aware of: long-form generation ( > 1k tokens) will reduce tokens/sec for other concurrent requests; if Acme expects a significant share of long-context runs, consider reserving a separate long-context pool or increasing committed tokens/sec accordingly.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call if you want me to walk procurement through the throughput_calcs_acme.xlsx workbook.

Thanks,
